reflection: Explain why one hot day does not describe a place’s whole climate.
title: Weather & Climate
description: Use explicit timescale clues to distinguish short-term weather from long-term climate patterns.
brief: Look for the time clue: conditions now, or a pattern over many years?

items.label: Usual wind direction over decades
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M22 19v70M13 90h20"/><path d="M22 22l65 14v16L22 52z" fill="#e2ac92"/><path d="M43 27v24M61 31v21M77 35v17" stroke="#fff4db" stroke-width="8"/></svg>
items.why: A prevailing wind pattern measured over decades is a climate pattern.

notes:
Focus: identify the timescale in each statement. Climate describes averages, variability and patterns over long periods; 30 years is commonly used for climate averages.

Content reference: Met Office — Our Climate.
